title: Angular Displacement, Velocity and Acceleration
notes: **Angular displacement $\theta$:** the angle through which a point on a rotating body moves, measured in radians. $\theta = s/r$, where $s$ is arc length and $r$ is radius.
**Angular velocity $\omega$:** rate of change of angular displacement. $\omega = d\theta/dt$. Units: rad/s.
**Angular acceleration $\alpha$:** rate of change of angular velocity. $\alpha = d\omega/dt$. Units: rad/s$^2$.
**Connection to linear motion:** $v = r\omega$ and $a_t = r\alpha$, where $v$ is tangential speed and $a_t$ is tangential acceleration.
**Direction:** angular velocity and acceleration are vectors along the axis of rotation, given by the right-hand rule.
